connection: Session 29 tested PayrollService with a real in-memory repository. Session 30 isolates ClockEntryService from IClockEntryRepository, first with a hand-written recording fake and then with Moq.
objectives: Explain how a test double isolates one class from a collaborator.
Build a small recording fake that supplies state and records an interaction.
Use Moq to configure the same repository boundary and verify a save call.
Choose between a real collaborator, fake, stub, and mock based on the evidence a test needs.

visuals.title: Isolation puts one class under the lens
visuals.explanation: ClockEntryService is the unit under test. A controlled IClockEntryRepository replaces storage so repository behavior cannot obscure the service decision.

visuals.title: A fake is working test code
visuals.explanation: The recording fake implements the real interface, returns configured values, and records saved entries in ordinary C# members the test can inspect.

visuals.title: Moq configures and verifies
visuals.explanation: Setup supplies the repository response. Verify checks that SaveClockEntry received the expected ClockEntry exactly once.

visuals.title: Choose the evidence, then the double
visuals.explanation: Use a real collaborator when it is fast and deterministic, a hand-written fake when state makes the behavior clear, and Moq when configuration or interaction verification is the clearest evidence.

preQuiz.prompt: What is isolated in a ClockEntryService unit test?
options: Every class from its own methods
preQuiz.explanation: The test controls IClockEntryRepository so it can focus on ClockEntryService behavior.

preQuiz.prompt: What makes a recording fake different from production storage?
options: It implements the contract with small deterministic test behavior
preQuiz.explanation: A fake is a test implementation of the same interface.

options: Evidence that a configured interaction occurred
preQuiz.explanation: Verify checks a specific collaborator call; assertions are still chosen by the test author.

concept.title: A test double replaces a collaborator
paragraphs: ClockEntryService is constructed with IClockEntryRepository. A unit test can supply a controlled implementation of that interface so the test exercises the service decision without depending on repository storage behavior.

Test double is the umbrella term. A stub supplies answers, a fake has a small working implementation, and a mock is commonly configured to verify interactions. Teams sometimes use these words loosely, so focus on the role the object performs.

concept.title: State evidence and interaction evidence answer different questions
paragraphs: A recording fake can expose LastSavedEntry and SaveCallCount. Assertions inspect that recorded state to prove what the service asked the collaborator to do.
Moq can express the same boundary with Setup and Verify. Setup controls what GetOpenClockEntry returns. Verify checks that SaveClockEntry received a matching ClockEntry exactly once.

concept.title: Isolation does not mean mocking everything
paragraphs: Session 29 correctly used the real in-memory repository because it was fast, deterministic, and part of the behavior being exercised. Session 30 replaces the repository because the new question is specifically how ClockEntryService collaborates through its interface.

Use the smallest double that makes the required evidence clear. A hand-written fake is often easier to debug; Moq is valuable when several responses must be configured or an interaction must be verified precisely.
concept.code: // Choose the boundary from the test question, not from habit.

concept.title: Read Moq one expression at a time
paragraphs: Mock<IClockEntryRepository> is a configurable wrapper. repository.Object is the IClockEntryRepository passed to production code.

It.Is<ClockEntry>(entry => ...) describes the argument that must match. Times.Once states the required call count. These expressions do not call the production method; they describe the verification Moq performs afterward.
concept.code:
Mock<IClockEntryRepository> repository = new();
IClockEntryRepository collaborator = repository.Object;

lab.title: Isolate ClockEntryService with Two Test-Double Styles
lab.objective: Test the same clock-in collaboration first with a recording fake and then with Moq, comparing the evidence each style provides.
lab.task: Prove that TryCLockIn returns true and saves one new entry when no open entry exists, without using the real repository implementation.
lab.startingCondition: Session 29 added permanent tests. ClockEntryService already depends on IClockEntryRepository, and the learner test project does not yet reference Moq.

labs.title: Isolate with a Recording Fake
labs.objective: Implement a minimal IClockEntryRepository fake and use its recorded state to verify ClockEntryService collaboration.
labs.task: Test the successful TryCLockIn path without ClockEntryRepository.

instructions.text: In project tests/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain.Tests, create ClockEntryServiceTests.cs. Declare public sealed class ClockEntryServiceTests in the global namespace used by the learner repository.

Inside ClockEntryServiceTests, before its final closing brace, declare private sealed class RecordingClockEntryRepository implementing IClockEntryRepository. Keep the helper's complete opening and closing braces inside the braces of ClockEntryServiceTests. Do not place it after the outer class has closed.

checkAfter.question: Which class is allowed to name this private nested helper?
checkAfter.answer: ClockEntryServiceTests can name it. Nesting keeps this test-only fake beside the tests and prevents other classes from treating it as a reusable test API.

instructions.text: Ask the editor to identify the three IClockEntryRepository members. Give SaveClockEntry an empty body, make GetEmployeeClockEntries return an empty ClockEntry sequence, and make GetOpenClockEntry temporarily return null. Keep these temporary implementations warning-free.

Inside the fake, add readable and settable ClockEntry? OpenEntryToReturn. Change GetOpenClockEntry so it returns that property. This property lets each test control the repository's answer without real storage.
Add readable ClockEntry? LastSavedEntry and int SaveCallCount properties whose setters are private. Change SaveClockEntry so it stores the clockEntry parameter and increments SaveCallCount.
instructions.purposeAfter: The fake now has a tiny notebook: it supplies the arranged answer and keeps a receipt of what the service later asks it to save. The service remains the class under test; the fake is only controlled test equipment.

checkAfter.question: Which object are you testing, and which object records the save call?
checkAfter.answer: ClockEntryService is under test. RecordingClockEntryRepository records the call so the test can inspect what the service did.

instructions.text: Inside ClockEntryServiceTests but outside the nested fake, type Fact method TryCLockIn_WhenNoOpenEntryExists_SavesEntryAndReturnsTrue. Give it a public void signature with no parameters and an empty body.
Inside the test method, create an explicitly typed RecordingClockEntryRepository named repository. Create an explicitly typed ClockEntryService named service and pass repository to its constructor.

checkAfter.question: Why does the test keep the variable as RecordingClockEntryRepository instead of IClockEntryRepository?
checkAfter.answer: The service only needs the interface, but the test needs the fake's extra LastSavedEntry and SaveCallCount receipt properties.

instructions.text: Create an explicitly typed DateTime named clockIn for August 15, 2026 at 9:00 AM. Remember the constructor order: year, month, day, hour, minute, second.
Act exactly once: call the real TryCLockIn spelling on service with employee ID 1 and clockIn. Store the returned bool in an explicitly typed variable named result.
instructions.purposeAfter: The arrangement is complete: the fake's default nullable answer means no open entry exists. This single call now runs the real service behavior; the next step checks both what it reported and what it requested.

instructions.text: Assert that result is true, repository.SaveCallCount equals 1, and repository.LastSavedEntry is not null. Then assert that the recorded entry's EmployeeId equals 1 and its ClockIn equals clockIn.

Run only TryCLockIn_WhenNoOpenEntryExists_SavesEntryAndReturnsTrue and review the passing name. Use the IDE test runner or the supplied CLI filter. If VS Code does not display the test after a successful build, refresh Testing, run Test: Refresh Tests, then reload the window if needed. Use dotnet test --list-tests to distinguish command-line discovery from a stale editor view.

labs.title: Express the Same Boundary with Moq
labs.objective: Configure IClockEntryRepository with Moq and verify the service's save interaction precisely.
labs.task: Test the same successful clock-in behavior so the two double styles can be compared fairly.

instructions.text: In the learner test-project csproj, add Moq version 4.20.72. Restore and build the test project before writing Moq syntax.
instructions.code:
dotnet add tests/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain.Tests/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain.Tests.csproj package Moq --version 4.20.72
dotnet build tests/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain.Tests/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain.Tests.csproj --configuration Release

instructions.text: At the top of ClockEntryServiceTests.cs, add using Moq. Inside the test class, type Fact method TryCLockIn_WhenNoOpenEntryExists_VerifiesSaveWithMoq.
Arrange Mock<IClockEntryRepository> named repository. Use Setup so GetOpenClockEntry for employee 1 returns a nullable ClockEntry value of null. Pass repository.Object to ClockEntryService.
instructions.purposeAfter: Moq now supplies the same controlled answer as the fake: no open entry exists. repository.Object is the interface implementation consumed by ClockEntryService; the next steps exercise and verify the service decision.

instructions.text: Create a fixed DateTime, then Act once by calling TryCLockIn for employee 1. Store the bool result.
Assert that the result is true. Then Verify SaveClockEntry with It.Is<ClockEntry> matching employee ID 1 and the fixed ClockIn value, and require Times.Once.

Compare the tests before running: the fake exposes recorded state in ordinary members, while Moq describes the expected interaction with Verify. Neither approach changes ClockEntryService production code.
instructions.purposeAfter: Both tests isolate the same service boundary and prove the same requirement with different evidence styles. The focused run now checks that both remain readable and pass together.

instructions.text: Run all ClockEntryServiceTests. Then build the Release solution and run the complete suite with --no-build. Open both Solution Reveals only after validation passes.
instructions.code:
dotnet test tests/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain.Tests/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain.Tests.csproj --configuration Release --filter FullyQualifiedName~ClockEntryServiceTests
dotnet build PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release
dotnet test PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release --no-build

lab.expectedBehavior: Both focused tests pass. Each proves that ClockEntryService returns true and requests one correctly populated save when no open entry exists.
lab.validation: dotnet test tests/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain.Tests/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain.Tests.csproj --configuration Release --filter FullyQualifiedName~ClockEntryServiceTests && dotnet build PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release && dotnet test PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release --no-build

postQuiz.prompt: Why can both tests omit ClockEntryRepository?
options: ClockEntryService depends on the IClockEntryRepository contract
postQuiz.explanation: Constructor injection allows either controlled implementation to satisfy the contract.

postQuiz.prompt: What evidence does the recording fake expose?
options: Recorded state such as LastSavedEntry and SaveCallCount
postQuiz.explanation: The fake stores interaction evidence in ordinary members.

options: When configuration or precise interaction verification is clearer
postQuiz.explanation: Choose Moq for the evidence and complexity of the boundary, not by habit.

reflections: Which part of each test isolates ClockEntryService from repository behavior?
Which test would be easier to debug without knowing a library API?
What additional repository scenarios would make Moq configuration more valuable?
whatBreaks: Using the real repository would mix service collaboration with storage behavior. Removing the fake's recording members loses state evidence. Removing Moq Verify allows the test to pass without proving the save interaction.
summary: A test double replaces a collaborator so a unit test can focus on one class. A recording fake provides explicit working test code and state evidence; Moq provides concise configuration and interaction verification. Neither is automatically superior—choose the smallest tool that makes the required evidence clear.
